campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine: Rank by fastest progress: model capability and validation first, then changes that make every later landing cheaper, then cleanup; owner-blocked and long-horizon rows last. Consolidate duplicated logic into fewer general components rather than adding instrumentation or frameworks; net AST nodes stay flat or fall, and the clone and harness ratchets hold the floor. Delete stale data and consolidate objects to reduce surface and improve robustness and efficiency: reviewed source lives in git, derived records in OvergoDB, process state in .overgo-runtime, and nothing a tool or evidence depends on lives in tmp. A consolidation row is done only when it deletes the implementations it replaces: test the shared owner's contract, keep only meaningful caller integration checks, retire tests of deleted wrappers, and report net production and test code removed, repeated executions eliminated, gate wall time and peak memory on comparable changes. Across the 197 first-parent commits to 2026-09-23, production Go grew about 9,000 net lines and tests about 11,600. OvergoDB keeps its core -- immutable content, a durable journal, aliases, rebuildable projections -- and the repository simplifies how it uses it, in order: integrity and blocking defects, one publication path, bounded queries, one record per transition, bounded memory, declared storage policy, then bounded segments. Store rows report bytes and records added per landing, records scanned per query, open and replay time, writer wait, peak memory and compaction write volume. No new model family, workflow, optimizer or orchestration framework without an owner request. A step's verify is its machine check; a check whose prerequisite cannot run records UNAVAILABLE, not a pass. depends_on names real producers. GUI and audio keep their lanes; master runs as master-lead. docs/plan.json is the only live plan. Improvement is what the user-facing scorecard measures (owner 2026-09-27): a row states the user-visible effect it predicts, naming a scorecard metric where it can, and work that moves only internal metrics states why it exists. Consolidation onto shared paths is how one fix reaches every model.

items.title: Move models, datasets and the store out of the module folder

steps.title: Move models, datasets and the store out of the module folder
steps.verify: test ! -e models && test ! -e datasets && test ! -e overgodb-store
steps.rationale: Measured 2026-09-27: go test's cache rechecks every path a test opens or stats inside the module folder. models/, datasets/ and overgodb-store/ live there, and resolving a path to them stats the repository root (925 times in one audioparity run). So a store write or a replaced root file re-runs every evidence suite with no code change: audioparity took 593 s in af56be31b and about 12.5 min in d836b7deb, after a root file was rewritten. Paths outside the module are never rechecked. Move: wait until no test uses the folders; rename the three into C:/Users/jeffm/overgo-data (same drive, seconds); point OVERGO_DATA_ROOT, OVERGO_AUDIO_REFERENCE_STORE and local-models.json there; repin the records that hold absolute paths under C:/Users/jeffm/overgo (grep finds them); land once, when the suites re-run one last time. Afterwards they re-run only when their code changes. Left over: about 25 root stats from tests that run git or go in the repository.

items.title: A slow landing is a defect: remove or speed up what makes it slow

steps.title: A slow landing is a defect: remove or speed up what makes it slow
steps.rationale: Owner 2026-09-27: a landing that takes more than about a minute is wrong (the number is a stand-in; the point is that slowness is a defect to remove, not a cost to accept). Measured today on the blocking path: the device and webui lanes (about 5 min whenever a change reaches them; removed from the landing with stop-state-out-of-store and run on the schedule), live-evidence acceptance suites re-running on any store write or dependency change (audioparity 376 s, cmd/compatibility 192 s, capabilityruntime 122 s, modelintake 119 s), cmd/gate's own landing test 61 s, commanddoc 32 s, vet up to 23 s. The gate's measured line names a landing over the budget and its slowest stages (a measurement; refusing after the run would only waste it), and each such landing's cause becomes the next fix: take it off the blocking path, make it fast, or delete it. Nothing joins the blocking path that breaks the budget for a narrow change. Owner 2026-09-27: unnecessary testing is a failure to fix, throughout: a check runs only when the change can alter its verdict. Done with stop-state-out-of-store: the lanes left the blocking path, and a change to the plan alone runs only the row's verify. Left: vet over the whole module on every landing (scope it to the changed packages and their importers), live-evidence suites (landing-hermetic-tests), and the slow checks that are relevant but slow (cmd/gate's own landing test, commanddoc).

items.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path

steps.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path
steps.rationale: Owner review 2026-09-27. Measured: 088a4774c's test stage re-ran 17 suites for 6 min 56 s (audioparity 376 s, cmd/compatibility 192 s, capabilityruntime 122 s, modelintake 119 s, server 71 s) because plan -stop had written a record into the live store at 17:56:23; the next plan-only landing, with no store write before it, ran 4 packages in 40 s. Suites that read the live store re-run on every store write, and their verdict depends on the machine's store rather than the commit. The gate runs go test with OVERGO_DATA_ROOT pointing at an empty scratch directory and OVERGO_AUDIO_REFERENCE_STORE unset (construction: no test can reach the live store through the environment); the 16 test files that name the store by path (overgodb-store, gitauthority.CanonicalOvergoDBDirectory) become hermetic on fixtures or scratch stores, or move off the landing path to the scheduled scorecard and validate, where live-store checks belong. Predicted effect: landings stop paying for store writes; a narrow landing's test stage stays near a minute. Measured 2026-09-27 before starting: with the data root pointed at an empty directory, 133 tests in 77 files across 12 packages fail (cmd/compatibility 32 files, internal/audioparity 19, internal/evaluation 10, speechsynth, server and others): retained-evidence acceptance tests and a few live model-file tests. They re-run when the evidence changes, which is correct; the measured 7-minute landing came from a control record (plan -stop) written into the evidence store, which stop-state-out-of-store removes. Moving them means splitting mixed files across 12 packages and a scheduled evidence run. Do it only if dev-loop measurement shows real evidence writes costing landings. Re-raised 2026-09-27 under landing-wall-budget: the four slowest suites a landing re-runs are these, and they re-run on dependency changes as well as store writes, so the stop-file fix alone does not bring landings under the budget.

items.title: Refuse production growth beyond the row's declared budget

steps.title: Refuse production growth beyond the row's declared budget
steps.rationale: Owner review 2026-09-27: prose rules against growth did not bind; this week's scorecard rows added 586 Go lines with no row declaring it. A diff rule in internal/landing/rules.go counts production Go AST nodes the change adds against HEAD (tests, testdata and generated files excluded; no baseline or ledger) and refuses growth beyond the landed row's plan Budget, whose default is zero: a row without a budget must pay its additions with deletions. A capability row declares its growth in plan data before the work. Keep the rule small; it is itself held to its budget.

items.title: Cut the scorecard slice back to what landings use

steps.title: Cut the scorecard slice back to what landings use
steps.rationale: Owner review 2026-09-27: the per-landing slice grew in three steps (ee13bdab2, de597cde9, 1cef3d9d9) to a multi-document protocol with crash continuation, per-slice HEAD blame, A B B A pairing and prose prediction parsing, for one document, and no real landing has used the pairing or the blame. Cut it back to what landings use: one inference slice, unpaired, its outputs and peak-device-memory compared with the newest measurement of its identity, one trailer. Per-modality coverage and paired timing belong to the scheduled scorecard, off the landing path. Rebuild a piece only when a real landing needs it. Make it a deletion with net production lines falling; the doctrine's prediction-naming sentence and SQA-019's prose parsing go with the pairing, and SQA-042 is moot once the gate no longer refuses on slice failures.

items.title: Stop the projection activation failing a quarter of its serving attempts

steps.title: Stop the projection activation failing a quarter of its serving attempts
steps.rationale: Found 2026-09-27 by the user scorecard (validate -scorecard): gemma-4-E4B-it's projection activation (recipe 93a7a292) failed 324 of 1,296 serving attempts with execution_failed and 324 more were cancelled, all at zero output tokens in one environment. Its observations also record task inference under the projection recipe (internal/server/server_admin.go servingIdentity), which is how the first scorecard draft charged them to the inference row. Find what drives these attempts and why they fail, fix the cause, and record the projection task; the scorecard's failure cell for the row is the predicted effect. Ranked 2026-09-27 as the first user-visible fix: gemma-4-E4B-it's projection recipe fails 324 of 1,296 serving attempts (25%) with 324 cancelled. A small hand change with its predicted failure-rate drop.

items.title: Unify prefill policy where reference parity permits

steps.title: Unify prefill policy where reference parity permits
steps.rationale: One policy from weight representation, column count and parity/cost evidence; keep precise staging where f16 cannot meet the bound. Measure the fp8 12B prompt-rate gap (1646 vs bf16 2850) on identical inputs. Accept kernel parity, scoped regression and before/after rate and memory curves. Moved up 2026-09-27 (owner): consolidation is what produces unintended improvement -- a speed-up or fix on one shared prefill path reaches every model on it. Judge it by how many models its shared path serves, measured on the scorecard. 2026-09-27: do this as behaviour-preserving transformations with known effect wherever possible (deadcode, gopls inline/rename/remove-unused-parameter, go fix, small go/ast programs) rather than hand edits, proven by compile, tests and the scorecard slice reading outputs identical; hand edits only where behaviour must change, each small and with its predicted effect.

items.title: Remove costly execution duplication behind the regression gate

steps.title: Remove costly execution duplication behind the regression gate
steps.rationale: Duplicate excess is 9927 nodes; bind a strictly lower target before starting. Pick a real duplicated CUDA or inference mechanism by cost, preserve accepted behavior, and lower docs/clone_baseline.json through clone-census. Moving or splitting duplication is not acceptance. Moved up 2026-09-27 (owner): one execution core means a fix for one model reaches all of them. Judge it by how many models its shared path serves, measured on the scorecard. 2026-09-27: same method as simplify-prefill-paths: tool-driven, behaviour-preserving transformations proven by the slice's outputs identical; hand edits only for intended behaviour changes.

items.title: Give each landing command stream one owner

steps.title: Give each landing command stream one owner
steps.rationale: SQA-035 (open), confirmed 2026-09-27: landing.run gives stdout io.MultiWriter(&output, &combined) and stderr &combined, and processcontrol serializes the two drains only when both streams share one sink (supervisor.go lockedWriter), so two goroutines write one bytes.Buffer, and stdout is retained twice. One owner per stream: stdout for the result, a bounded diagnostic tail for the error; stream go test events through the existing parser where the whole output is not needed. No logging framework.

items.title: Commit exactly the bytes the gate validated, and recover the row after a failed commit

steps.title: Commit exactly the bytes the gate validated, and recover the row after a failed commit
steps.rationale: SQA-034 (P1, open): the landing validates the dirty tree and then commits whatever the tree holds at commit time, and a commit that fails after the plan advance can lose the row. Bind validation and the row verifier to the exact prepared candidate bytes, and make the plan advance recoverable against the expected parent. Keep the post-fix ship-set re-read (ee13bdab2). Reuse the existing git and process owners and small landing fixtures; no ledger, no authority service.

items.title: Move every rule to its cheapest deterministic level and keep the list short

steps.title: Move every rule to its cheapest deterministic level and keep the list short
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27: sort each rule (the small gate's rules, the repoanalysis tree tests, scripts/guard.sh, the doctrine prose) by the cheapest level that makes it deterministic: construction (types and API shape), a diff rule against HEAD, an auto-fix inside the landing, a tool guard, a behaviour test, or a few injected lines of judgement. A rule that asks the agent for justification text is bookkeeping: move it up or down. Candidates: no .py files and no time.Sleep around input-dependent work as diff rules; timers and store access by construction. Delete a rule that never fires or fires only wrongly; keep about 10-15; rule code counts against net production lines. Observed 2026-09-27 (user-scorecard/define): the gate's fix stage and a worker's go fix both stale derived files that pin source bytes -- compatibility claim identities (cmd/compatibility -refresh-identities) and the API manifest (cmd/api-manifest -update) -- so a landing refuses at test and reruns. Per the ladder, regenerating derived files is an auto-fix: run those regenerators inside the landing after fix, as format and fix already run. Re-ranked 2026-09-27 behind the landing rows: a rule that false-positives stalls every unattended landing (the owner's current focus). SQA-039 (the zero-fallback rule refuses lazy fallbacks that cmp.Or would change) and SQA-036 (the export rule counts text mentions as consumers) land here.

items.title: Run or delete tests no lane enables

steps.title: Run or delete tests no lane enables
steps.rationale: From consolidation-inventory (2026-09-24): 283 OVERGO_* environment reads sit in tests; 151 names appear only in tests and 145 of those are documented nowhere. 130 test functions (about 12,000 lines) skip unless a variable is set, and the lanes set only OVERGO_CUDA_TEST, OVERGO_WEBUI_LANE, OVERGO_WEBUI_LANE_SCREENS and OVERGO_BROWSER, so about 82 of them (about 5,800 lines, heaviest in internal/inference, adaptiveparity and projector) never run in any gate. Owner direction 2026-09-24: training and inference validation is the point of overgo, so give each a lane that runs it, with its model or data declared. Delete only a test a named running test supersedes. The same holds for modeltest-tagged suites no lane runs, such as seq2seq's GSM8K training suite. The probe is tmp/envgate_probe.go. Done when TestEveryTestGateIsSetByALane holds. Re-ranked 2026-09-27 behind the landing rows: SQA-037 (module-file changes can bypass the device and browser lanes), SQA-028 and SQA-023 are gate correctness defects this row owns.

items.title: Shrink the plan tool to plain data

steps.title: Shrink the plan tool to plain data
steps.rationale: Owner review 2026-09-27: with the completion rules gone and rows plain data, the tool needs roughly -next, -status, -add, -setverify, -verify and -stop. internal/plan is 3.2k lines plus 3.8k of tests and cmd/plan 2.6k plus tests; dispatchreadiness and lanestore exist only for cmd/plan. Delete the old machinery's flags (-admit-proposal, -charge-exploration, -grant-exploration, -contain, -budget, -assign, -record-lease, -locality-schedule, -history and its phases, -prepare-merge now that a merge is git merge --no-ff --no-commit then a landing) and what only they use. Target 6-8k lines with tests. Re-ranked 2026-09-27 behind the landing rows: SQA-038 (a landed merge is invisible to the loop's progress check) and the plan-advance half of SQA-034 sit in the plan tool this row shrinks.

items.title: One user-facing scorecard across every model, the definition of improvement

steps.title: Run the full scorecard on a schedule and publish it with its deltas
steps.rationale: The full scorecard, every model and every cell, runs on a schedule (the machine is shared: it takes the device claim) and publishes one record with deltas against the previous run. It is the fitness the unattended loop optimizes (loop-fitness-scorecard). From the per-modality design (2026-09-27), the scheduled scorecard owns what a per-landing slice cannot afford or cannot run: tabular (tabfm, 78 s for four golden cases), vqa (RxBrain, 25 GB device load, 21 s a run, and its image read from the store it executes against), projection (no capability executor; the user path is inference with a projector, 15 GB and up), training (sessions and checkpoints), activity-detection with its first activation, every model that is not its task's smallest, and scratch seeding for latent-image profiles. 2026-09-27: per-modality-tasks, load-split and typed-predictions are retired from the landing path with the slice's simplification; the scheduled scorecard owns every modality's smallest-model run (through the catalog executor on a scratch store, as the per-modality design worked out) and any load-versus-execution split it needs. Since stop-state-out-of-store (2026-09-27) the device, webui and model-journey lanes are off the landing path: the schedule runs them, and a failure becomes a row.

steps.title: Fill the scorecard: the absorbed benchmark and validation work
steps.rationale: Absorbs, 2026-09-27: model-regression-baseline (full text catalog, both prompt shapes, required contexts, rates and peak/retained memory under budgets, accepted record ids pinned), benchmark-completion (compare only cells whose checkpoint, precision, split, shots, template, scoring and extraction agree; keep the 100-case MMLU label; TestAcceptedPublishedComparison rejects omitted cells, duplicates, stale identities and failed outcomes), final-model-validation (a bounded long-lived server run: concurrency, context grow and shrink, cancellation, failure, reload, VRAM plateauing within budget), benchmark-27b (operator only, -budget 3h per launch, resuming exact remaining cases; the row reads completed evidence and never starts the pass), gemma-12b-accuracy (OWNER DECISION still open: download the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it? the 12B FP8 twins score 0.5-1.2 nats per token worse than E4B on the guard corpus while overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers reference, so the suspect is the third-party quant) and validate-all-models (RAE is the remaining unvalidated model, rae-generation-path). Done when every model's row has every cell measured or carrying a stated reason.

items.title: Make pending owner decisions typed plan data with a one-click inbox

steps.title: Make pending owner decisions typed plan data with a one-click inbox
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27. Decisions sit inside rationale prose ("OWNER DECISION: ..."): the compatibility binding waited 09-21 to 09-27, the Gemma 12B bf16 download since 09-24, and an unattended loop stalls quietly on them. A decision becomes typed plan data: the question, the options, a recommendation and the rows it blocks. plan -decisions lists them; the GUI shows them as a short inbox answered with one click; decision latency becomes visible and measured. Migrate the open ones (the 12B bf16 and RAE downloads, redundant store backups, the self-improvement cluster's cut).

items.title: Promote master to main only when the scorecard holds, and revert on a regression

steps.title: Promote master to main only when the scorecard holds, and revert on a regression
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27. main mirrors master, so unattended changes reach users directly. Promote master to main automatically only when the scorecard shows no regression, and revert automatically when one appears, so users see only improvements and nobody has to watch releases. Until this lands, pushing stays on the owner's explicit request.

items.title: Report dead references in memory and hook text at session start

steps.title: Report dead references in memory and hook text at session start
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27: prose drifts from code mechanically (80% of the gate manual described deleted tools; closure-scan, plan -history -phases and the deferred lanes stayed in the doctrine after their deletion). At session start the hook scans the memory files and its own doctrine text for cmd/<name>, -<flag> of a named command, Test<Name> and repository paths, and prints each that no longer exists. Cheap, deterministic, no ledger.

items.title: Onboard a model from its directory to validated with one command

steps.title: Onboard a model from its directory to validated with one command
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27. Today onboarding is about six steps, each with a trap: recipe spec needs git status run first on a copied model repo, recipe verify takes JSON on stdin, goldens are copied from a mismatch error, then activate, the benchmark publish and the guard. One command from a model directory to validated, and one metric beside the scorecard's setup steps: the share of models supported by declaration alone, with no model-specific code. Each new model then becomes unintended improvement.

items.title: Fold per-modality commands into route tables

steps.title: Fold per-modality commands into route tables
steps.rationale: Consolidation round 1, refactor 5. 102 commands (25 at the start): 10 train probes, 9 lanes, 6 parity or oracle commands, 14 model-file tools, 5 store tools. Fold them into route tables: the probes become routes of cmd/train -route (docs/training_routes.json, one objective mode for every objective kind: forecast, tabular and text fold into cmd/train -objective), the lanes become cmd/gate -lane, parity tools become cmd/validate -parity, the gguf and inspect tools become cmd/gguf subcommands, the overgodb tools cmd/overgodb subcommands. One model loader and one registry lookup for training, inference and validation. Every trainer stays reachable (capabilities are not dead code); only entry points collapse. Absorbs simplify-command-surface's command half. Done when TestTrainRoutesEveryProbe proves each former probe trains through cmd/train. Owner review 2026-09-27: 97 commands, about 40 of them under 100 lines of code, many thin wrappers. Lanes are no longer cmd/gate -lane: the lanes the gate does not call go in lane-commands-folded. Moved up 2026-09-27 (owner): fewer parts means fewer ways to fail, which users notice as reliability.

items.title: Drive the unattended loop by the scorecard: its gaps are the work, its held-out cells the fitness

steps.title: Chain strategy, experiment, held-out fitness and rollout promotion into one guarded path
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27: chain the existing model-loop parts (internal/loop strategy, experiment, held-out fitness, rollout promotion) into one path, with the circuit breaker and rollback as guards, whose fitness is the scorecard's held-out cells.

steps.title: Feed plan -admit-proposal from scorecard regressions and the weakest metrics
steps.rationale: A scheduled scorecard regression, or the weakest metric, becomes a typed proposal the unattended loop admits (plan -admit-proposal), so its work comes from what users feel. Keep the held-out rows high so the loop improves real quality rather than its own tests.

items.title: Turn real serving failures into findings and scorecard cells (local, opt-in)

steps.title: Turn real serving failures into findings and scorecard cells (local, opt-in)
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27. Benchmarks miss what users hit. The server already records serving observations per request (time to first token via the prefill sample, outcome, peak device memory); make the recording an explicit local opt-in, feed the scorecard from it, and turn every crash or refusal into a finding automatically, so real failures become the unattended loop's work supply beside the benchmark's gaps.

items.title: Measure the improver: wall, refusals, rework and cost per landed row, and the worst-case landing

steps.title: Measure the improver: wall, refusals, rework and cost per landed row, and the worst-case landing
steps.rationale: Owner recommendation 2026-09-27. The loop's own speed decides how fast users see improvement. Beside the user scorecard, report from git (Landed-Row trailers and the Measured by the gate lines) and the loop's own records: wall time per landed row, refused landings per landed row, rework (rows reopened or reverted), agent cost per landed row, and the worst-case landing -- a change to a widely imported package such as internal/tensor or internal/artifact that invalidates most of the test cache. That is the next speed cliff: today's one-minute landings are narrow changes.

items.title: Gate DPO approval on held-out preference pairs

steps.title: Gate DPO approval on held-out preference pairs
steps.rationale: Preference held-out slice (design 2026-09-24): the web UI training workspace runs DPO with no held-out check. Score held-out preference pairs with ScorePreferenceTargets from policy and reference sequence scores, judge against the reference, and gate the workspace's approval on the verdict. GRPO has no target scorer yet, so name that as its own follow-up. Done when TestPreferenceWorkspaceScoresHeldOutPairs refuses approval without a held-out gain and grants it with one.

items.title: Judge text generation objectives on held-out text targets

steps.title: Judge text generation objectives on held-out text targets
steps.rationale: The text target scorers (CompileTextTargetPlan, ScoreTextTargets: continuation likelihood, generated answer, structured validity, OCR fields, VQA rules) restored in c99544b6 judge what a text model generates, not next-token accuracy, so token-accuracy objectives do not use them. Wire them for objectives whose output is generated text: run the base and trained model's generation over held-out prompts, score with the scorer the objective declares, and judge through a text target verdict. Unlimited-OCR (OCR fields) and a generated-answer objective are the first users. Done when TestGenerationObjectiveApprovesOnHeldOutAnswers approves a tiny generation objective on a held-out answer gain.

items.title: Approve media objectives on held-out signal quality

steps.title: Approve media objectives on held-out signal quality
steps.rationale: Media held-out slice (design 2026-09-24): CompileMediaTargetPlan and ScoreMediaTargets need output artifacts, oracles and verifier profiles, and generation through mediacapability takes minutes per record on CUDA. Wire audio-snr (Pocket-TTS) first, then image and video PSNR (Krea-2-Turbo, Wan2.1), scoring a bounded held-out subset whose size the objective declares. Done when TestMediaObjectiveApprovesOnHeldOutGain approves a tiny synthetic audio objective on a held-out SNR gain.

items.title: Approve a TabFM objective on held-out rows of a real table

steps.title: Approve a TabFM objective on held-out rows of a real table
steps.rationale: Owner 2026-09-25: prove held-out approval on real checkpoints one model at a time, smallest first; TabFM-1.0 classification is first (staged at models/tabfm-1.0.0-pytorch; its location is resolved by identity, not assumed). One run is the row's acceptance, the device-lane evidence, the model-journey check and the training-validation verdict at once. Register a tabular objective over a real table dataset with a group split, train through cmd/train -objective, and approve on held-out label accuracy. Follows the consolidation rounds. Done when TestTabFMObjectiveApprovesOnHeldOutRows records a passed verdict on the real checkpoint.

items.title: Keep goldens in git under one provenance manifest and delete their Python generators

steps.title: Keep goldens in git under one provenance manifest and delete their Python generators
steps.rationale: Owner direction 2026-09-26. 177 tracked goldens (4.3 MB, the largest about 1 MB) stay where they are in git -- fixtures/ and package testdata -- because git is the durable, pushed copy, the store is local and has been rebuilt, a golden in git never makes its test skip, and moving them would churn the tests and the records that pin them. What they lack is provenance. One manifest in fixtures/ records, for each golden, its upstream repository and commit, its checkpoint identity, its input digest and its own digest; TestGoldensHaveProvenance refuses a golden without an entry or whose bytes differ from it. The upstream output itself is kept, not just a parity verdict: kernels legitimately move numbers, and only the upstream output re-checks parity after each move without re-running Python, where comparing against overgo's own old output would stack tolerances. The Python generators are deleted -- internal/parity/testdata/make_olmoe_tiny.py and those in tmp (timesfm3_golden.py, dinov2_golden.py, generate_kimi_k3_rank_reference.py and their inputs) -- because the manifest names what to re-run if upstream ever changes; no Python is tracked. The store holds only a future golden too large for git; none is today.

items.title: Delete the reference-comparison packages whose ports goldens lock

steps.title: Delete the reference-comparison packages whose ports goldens lock
steps.rationale: Owner 2026-09-26: once a port is locked by goldens, the reference-comparison packages go. internal/adaptiveparity, cmd/sensenovaparity and cmd/vqaparity have no production importer; each is deleted once the comparisons it runs exist as committed goldens with provenance (goldens-provenance: goldens stay in git). internal/audioparity is not pure comparison -- internal/mediacapability and cmd/webui-lane import it for ASR qualification and election -- so its production part moves to its owner and only its comparison part goes. No new rule: done when go list no longer finds the three packages and the tree still builds and vets. Check: the reader census, since deleting the packages must leave none of their fixtures or testdata behind; done also when go list no longer finds them.

OWNER PERMISSION needed for the moves: the guard protects model directories.

items.title: Fold the media campaign's receipts into fewer committed records

items.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on

steps.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on
steps.rationale: Three sessions share one GPU. Preview servers started through launch.json hold the device while gate lanes time out behind them, and on 2026-09-23 a server of unknown origin was killed to free it. A served model should hold the same claim, so a lane waits for it and names it (01cbf544) instead of timing out. 2026-09-25: the device lane of 69368990 failed 'physical resource is already reserved' in devicemath while two other gate processes held the GPU, and passed unchanged on re-run; a claim every GPU user takes turns that into a wait with a named holder instead of a failed lane and a manual re-run. Found 2026-09-26: every CUDA context already takes the shared device claim (driver.ContextCreate calls processcontrol.ShareResource), so a served model holds it for its context's life, and a timed-out exclusive wait already names its holders (01cbf544, TestResourceWaitNamesItsHolders). What remains is proof, not mechanism: a device test that a served model's context holds the claim an exclusive reservation then waits on.

items.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it

steps.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it
steps.rationale: The overgo_vae lane (branch codex/overgo_vae, campaign overgo_rsi_with_vae, design docs/overgo_rsi_with_vae.md) runs the native-Go latent RSI and PEARL campaign with its own plan in its own worktree. Owner decision 2026-09-25: master takes the lane in parts that have a production consumer, not whole. Master ported the runtime part at e1ee1326fe2b (row vae-codec-stream-port: media.CodecChunkStream owning causal codec state, the Wan VAE host and CUDA encode and CUDA decode through it; the host streaming DecodeLatentVideo stays a test on master until it has a production caller); the ported files are byte-identical to the lane's, so merging master back is clean. DIRECTION FOR THE LANE when it merges master (master is in a consolidation-only phase: two birds with one stone, minimize to the maximum practical extent, no ledger where construction can prevent the object): (1) consumer first -- land each latent contract (representation latent state and codec, geometry, tensorstats resampling and robust scalars, media latent volume) together with its first production consumer; the first merge unit is first-latent-capability/existing-vae-inference-proof, and no export arrives without a caller; (2) no new record families -- express experimental evidence through the shared record table that automation-one-record-table builds instead of runrecord experimental_* families, and keep campaign-history adoption out of master's internal/plan; (3) reconcile pinned media runtime moves with a reviewed delta in docs/media_reviewed_deltas.json backed by a device receipt, never by narrowing TestReviewedDeltaRegistryExplainsTheTree; (4) never raise docs/clone_baseline.json -- the merged tree measured 7964 against master's 7991 while the lane raised it to 9970; (5) after merging master, drop the lane's testCodecChunkState copy in internal/media/codec_latent_test.go: master's TestCodecChunkStreamOwnsCausalState owns it; (6) keep evidence identities in compatibility.json refreshed from master's store, not the lane's. Master keeps its plan; any staged surface a later merge brings retires with this row. Done when the lane's campaign closeout has merged and TestVAECampaignClosedOut proves no staged entry names this row.

items.title: Page across several schemas by reading only the page

steps.title: Page across several schemas by reading only the page
steps.rationale: SQA-005: 8a77c2d8 made a single-schema document read proportional to its page, but a page across several schemas still merges history-sized candidate sets, and run browsing still counts the whole history on every request. Seek independently in each schema's sorted index and lazily merge only the candidates the page needs. For runs, reuse a count bound to the same store head, or make the total an explicit request, keeping the response contract. Include setup and allocation cost in the measurement. Done when TestMultiSchemaPageReadsOnlyThePage reads a two-schema page from a store holding many older documents and touches only a page-bounded number of them. Re-measure 2026-09-27 after gate-small-cutover: the gate's own records drive most store growth and evidence churn, so this row may no longer be needed. Kept 2026-09-27 after the records re-measure: store growth stopped with the old gate (86% of the last 3,558 commits were its records, 12% a test fixed in 944540a7; the sequence held at 63557 across four landings), but this is a read cost on the existing history, not a growth cost.

items.title: Defer decoding large store facets until first use, if opens are still slow

steps.title: Defer decoding large store facets until first use, if opens are still slow
steps.rationale: Re-measured 2026-09-24 after store-open-decode-cost (180a7a3c): an open takes about 1.05-1.5 s and allocates 1.8 GB; checkpoint decode is 56% of it (lineage 0.6 s) and replaying the 8,100 commits since the last checkpoint is 32%. Before that, 2026-09-22: a read-only open is 1.7 s, bounded by the largest decode (lineage 88.3 MB of 189 MB), with verification about 0.1 s. Laziness inside the facet fails (value receivers) and re-replaying the journal fails (shared file cursor). Defer at the store, which owns the lock: keep the verified payload and pending commits, apply on first load behind a double-checked write lock, and test that a deferred facet answers exactly as an eager one. Re-measure 2026-09-27 after gate-small-cutover: the gate's own records drive most store growth and evidence churn, so this row may no longer be needed. Kept 2026-09-27 after the records re-measure: growth stopped, so the open cost no longer rises, but every command and store-reading test still pays it once.
